blockers: No REST, GraphQL, or any programmatic API exists
No OpenAPI/Swagger specification or machine-readable interface documentation
No structured response formats (JSON/XML) - all output is raw HTML
info: Two user-facing endpoints exist: index.cfm (search/listing) and download.cfm (file retrieval), accessed via GET parameters

blockers: No standard authentication protocol (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, JWT, API keys, IAM)
risks: Session fixation vulnerability - no token rotation on login
No HTTPS - credentials transmitted in cleartext
ColdFusion Administrator password hardcoded in documentation
info: No authorization model - any authenticated user can access all documents

blockers: No idempotency keys or tokens on any operation
risks: No transaction management visible in code
State stored in ColdFusion server-side sessions tied to single instance
info: Single SQL Server instance - no distributed state concerns but no redundancy

blockers: No confirmation steps before destructive or high-impact actions
risks: No audit trail - document access and downloads are not logged
info: No content moderation or review processes

blockers: No application logging in the codebase
No distributed tracing or correlation IDs
risks: No metrics collection (request counts, error rates, latency)
info: .gitignore excludes *.log files suggesting runtime logs may exist, but no instrumentation in application code

blockers: SQL Injection in index.cfm - url.q concatenated directly into SQL
SQL Injection in download.cfm - url.id used without parameterization
Path Traversal in download.cfm - file paths constructed from DB values without sanitization
XSS in index.cfm - url.q rendered in HTML without encoding
risks: All infrastructure components are EOL with known unpatched CVEs
No input validation anywhere in the application

remediation_path: Expose a structured API (REST/GraphQL) with OpenAPI documentation
Implement standard authentication (OAuth 2.0/OIDC) with M2M support
Add idempotency keys for mutating operations
Add human-in-the-loop controls (approval workflows, rate limiting, confirmation steps)
Instrument observability (structured logging, distributed tracing, health checks, metrics)
Fix security vulnerabilities (parameterize SQL, validate inputs, enforce HTTPS)
Modernize platform off EOL software stack
